--- title: "Niger Drought Trigger Design" subtitle: "IRI Forecast-Based Anticipatory Action Trigger · 1998–2025" date: today date-format: "D MMMM YYYY" --- ## Overview This document describes the design of an anticipatory action trigger for drought in Niger, based on IRI seasonal forecast probabilities and an August rainfall observation. The trigger has **two independent arms** — either can fire to release early action: - **Forecast arm**: fires when any two consecutive monthly IRI forecasts (January–June) are both among the top 5 most elevated "below-normal" years in the historical record. - **Observation arm**: fires when early August rainfall is among the bottom 5 driest years. The trigger is calibrated against 28 years of data (1998–2025), targeting approximately a **1-in-3.5 year** combined return period. --- ## Data Three data sources are used: | Variable | Description | Period | |---|---|---| | IRI Jan–Jun | Monthly probability of below-normal JAS precipitation (%) | 1991–2025 | | Aug observation | August rainfall z-score (CHIRPS-based) | 1998–2025 | | JAS SPI | July–August–September SPI (validation outcome) | 1998–2024 | The IRI forecast probabilities are expressed as fractions (0–1) of the climatological below-normal tercile. The August observation is a standardised anomaly — lower (more negative) values indicate drier conditions. The beta regression trend models are **fit on the full 1991–2025 record** to maximise sample size for estimating the long-term climate shift. The trigger threshold design uses **1998–2025 only**, matching the period of reliable operational data. --- ## Detrending IRI seasonal forecast probabilities for below-normal precipitation show a declining trend over 1991–2025. This likely reflects the partial recovery of Sahelian rainfall since the 1970s–80s drought era, alongside improvements in the IRI model's baseline climatology. Without detrending, a historical percentile threshold would systematically favour recent years and underweight older drought signals. We apply a two-step detrending procedure: 1. **Beta regression** — fits a trend curve bounded to (0, 1), appropriate for probability data. Divides out the trend so the series fluctuates around a constant mean. 2. **Variance standardisation** — fits a linear model to the absolute residuals over time, then rescales so the spread is constant across years. The beta trend is fit on the **full historical record** (1991–2025); the variance model is also fit on all years. Both are then applied to the 1998–2025 analysis window. ### Detrending steps ::: {#cell-fig-detrend-steps .cell fig-height='18' fig-width='14' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Detrending pipeline for each forecast month. Blue = full-record beta trend; grey = raw observations. Col 1: mean-detrended series. Col 2: absolute residuals with linear spread fit. Col 3: fully detrended series.](index_files/figure-html/fig-detrend-steps-output-1.png){#fig-detrend-steps} ::: ::: ### Model fit summary ::: {#tbl-gof .cell tbl-cap='Beta trend and variance fit quality. β R²: Pearson r² between fitted trend and squeezed observations. The variance R² measures how much of the spread heteroscedasticity is explained by a linear trend in time. --- ## Forecast Skill ### JAS SPI timeseries ::: {#cell-fig-spi .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='10' execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![JAS SPI (July–August–September Standardised Precipitation Index), 1998–2024. Negative (red) bars indicate below-normal seasonal rainfall.](index_files/figure-html/fig-spi-output-1.png){#fig-spi} ::: ::: ### Correlation with IRI forecasts The plot below compares how strongly each monthly IRI forecast correlates with the JAS SPI outcome, before and after detrending. Negative correlations (plotted here as positive for readability) indicate that a higher "below-normal" forecast probability is associated with a drier season — a useful predictive signal. ::: {#cell-fig-corr .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='8' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Negative correlation between monthly IRI forecast and JAS SPI. Higher bars = stronger drought forecast skill. Detrending generally preserves or slightly improves skill.](index_files/figure-html/fig-corr-output-1.png){#fig-corr} ::: ::: ### ROC AUC — lower-tercile drought years The ROC AUC summarises how well each monthly forecast discriminates between drought years (JAS SPI below the lower tercile) and non-drought years. An AUC of 0.5 is no better than chance; 1.0 is perfect. ::: {#cell-fig-roc .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='8' execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![ROC AUC for each monthly IRI forecast against the binary outcome (JAS SPI below lower tercile). Values above 0.5 indicate useful forecast skill.](index_files/figure-html/fig-roc-output-1.png){#fig-roc} ::: ::: --- ## Trigger Design ### Parameters The trigger was designed over 28 years (1998–2025) using the **full historical record detrending model**. The selected thresholds fire in approximately 10 out of 28 years — a **1-in-2.9** combined return period. | Parameter | Value | |---|---| | Analysis period | 1998–2025 (28 years) | | Detrending model | Full historical record (1991–2025) | | Forecast arm: trigger years | Top 5 of 28 ≈ 17.9% | | Observation arm: trigger years | Bottom 5 of 28 ≈ 17.9% | | Total trigger years | 10 / 28 | | Combined return period | ~1-in-2.9 years | The **forecast arm** fires when any two *consecutive* monthly forecasts (e.g. Jan+Feb, Feb+Mar, …, May+Jun) are both in the top 5 years. Requiring consecutive months adds persistence, reducing false alarms from single-month spikes. The **observation arm** provides a safety net: it fires independently when the August rainfall observation is among the bottom 5 years, even if the forecast arm did not fire. ### Thresholds (detrended space) ::: {#tbl-thresh .cell tbl-cap='Trigger thresholds in fully detrended space. To apply the trigger in practice, we need the equivalent threshold in **raw forecast probability space** for each future year. The back-transformation inverts both detrending steps using the fitted models, accounting for the expected beta trend and spread at each year. Because the underlying trend in below-normal probabilities is declining, the raw threshold for 2026–2027 is **lower** than it would have been in the 1990s — the trigger will fire at a lower absolute forecast probability, reflecting the changed climatology. ::: {#cell-fig-backtr .cell fig-height='8' fig-width='14' execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Raw IRI forecast probabilities (grey) with beta trend (blue) and back-transformed trigger threshold (gold dashed). Red dots mark years that triggered in detrended space. Gold diamonds show the 2026 and 2027 threshold values.](index_files/figure-html/fig-backtr-output-1.png){#fig-backtr} ::: ::: ### Forward-looking thresholds The table below gives the trigger threshold in raw forecast probability space for 2026 and 2027. A monthly IRI below-normal probability **at or above** the value shown means that month contributes toward triggering the forecast arm (subject to the consecutive-month requirement). ::: {#tbl-future .cell tbl-cap='Back-transformed trigger thresholds for 2026 and 2027.
